identity.name: Sheikh Arfaz Ahamed
identity.headline: Developer — Web Tooling & Automation
identity.tagline: I build tools that check their own work before anyone else has to.

bio.short: Developer working on web tooling and automation. Most recently Portfolio Forge, a site generator that refuses to publish anything it has not verified first.
bio.long:
I like the part of software where correctness is mechanical, not argued about. Most of what I build is a version of the same idea: make the machine prove the thing works, so nobody has to take my word for it.

Portfolio Forge is the clearest example. Tools that ask a model to write a website from scratch are a coin flip, and the user is the one holding it. So Forge never generates a layout — it injects content into measured slots in a template that already builds, then verifies the result in a real browser at six breakpoints before a byte reaches GitHub.

That constraint is the interesting part. Generated sites rarely break because the CSS is wrong. They break because real content is a different size than the content the template was drawn for. No compiler catches that. A browser does.

projects.title: Portfolio Forge
projects.summary: Generates a portfolio from a pre-tested template, verifies it at six breakpoints, and deploys it to your own GitHub Pages.
projects.description: A Claude Code plugin that interviews you, writes your content into a template that already builds, and proves the result works before publishing it. Ten templates, each verified nightly in CI against a sparse profile and a full one. Every field has a measured character bound; every built site passes six gates — schema, build, runtime, layout, links and accessibility — at 350 to 1536px. Nothing is pushed to your GitHub until all six are green.
